title: Why Wall Street Can't Get Enough of This Dividend King
author: Reuben Gregg Brewer
description: AbbVie, a pharmaceutical company spun off from Abbott in 2013, maintains Dividend King status with an attractive 2.7% yield well above industry averages. Despite a high earnings payout ratio of 330%, the company's cash flow-based payout ratio of 60% indicates a sustainable dividend. AbbVie's strong portfolio includes blockbuster drugs like Botox and newer immunology treatments (Skyrizi and Rinvoq) that offset patent expirations. The company's recent $11 billion acquisition of Apogee further strengthens its pipeline in inflammatory and immunological diseases.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong dividend track record with attractive 2.7% yield, sustainable cash flow-based payout ratio of 60%, robust drug pipeline with successful replacements for expiring patents (Skyrizi, Rinvoq), differentiated Botox revenue stream, strategic acquisitions strengthening market position, and investment-grade balance sheet.
Mentioned as AbbVie's former parent company that spun off the subsidiary in 2013. No specific performance or outlook information provided in the article.
Acquisition target being purchased by AbbVie for $11 billion, bringing clinical-stage candidates in inflammatory and immunological diseases, which strengthens AbbVie's pipeline and market position.

title: 3 Reasons to Buy AbbVie Stock Like There's No Tomorrow
author: Prosper Junior Bakiny
description: AbbVie has demonstrated strong recovery after Humira's patent loss, with immunology drugs Skyrizi and Rinvoq exceeding sales expectations and not facing biosimilar competition until 2033. The company maintains a promising pipeline including weight-loss therapy ABBV-295 and acquired eczema treatment zumilokibart. AbbVie's Dividend King status with 203.5% dividend increases over the past decade and a 2.7% yield makes it an attractive long-term investment despite near-term headwinds from Humira decline and Imbruvica pricing pressure.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong revenue recovery post-Humira patent loss, exceptional performance of Skyrizi and Rinvoq exceeding management expectations, promising pipeline candidates (ABBV-295, zumilokibart), and exceptional dividend track record as a Dividend King with consistent increases over the past decade.
Mentioned only as AbbVie's former parent company for historical context regarding dividend history; no specific analysis or investment recommendation provided in the article.
Acquired by AbbVie for $10.9 billion; its key asset zumilokibart is positioned as a promising eczema treatment with differentiated dosing schedule that could strengthen AbbVie's immunology portfolio.

title: What This Apogee Insider Move Might Mean After a 247% Stock Run
author: Jonathan Ponciano
description: Apogee Therapeutics CEO Michael Henderson disposed of 95,046 shares, with 75,046 gifted to charity and 20,000 sold under a pre-established trading plan. Henderson retains 921,000 shares worth ~$123 million. The insider activity is not viewed as a red flag given the CEO's substantial remaining stake. Apogee's lead antibody candidate showed strong Phase 2 data for atopic dermatitis, with Phase 3 trials and head-to-head comparisons against Dupixent expected in late 2026. The company has $1.3 billion in cash funding operations into 2029.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong Phase 2 clinical data for lead candidate with durable responses, substantial cash runway through 2029, upcoming Phase 3 launch and competitive head-to-head trial readouts in late 2026 represent significant near-term catalysts. CEO's retention of $123 million in stock demonstrates confidence. 247% one-year stock performance reflects market optimism despite current net losses.

title: AbbVie Is Already a Dividend King. Here's Why the $10.9 Billion Apogee Deal Could Make It a Dynasty
author: Reuben Gregg Brewer
description: AbbVie, a Dividend King, is acquiring Apogee Therapeutics for $10.9 billion to strengthen its drug pipeline and maintain its dividend growth streak. The deal brings late-stage drug candidates like zumilokibart for atopic dermatitis and respiratory drugs, helping AbbVie replace revenue lost from Humira's patent expiration with newer products like Skyrizi and Rinvoq.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: The acquisition demonstrates AbbVie's strategic ability to maintain its Dividend King status by proactively replacing aging drugs with new candidates. The deal strengthens its pipeline in core therapeutic areas and positions the company for long-term dividend sustainability.

Being acquired by a major pharmaceutical company validates Apogee's drug candidates and provides resources for development. The acquisition offers shareholders liquidity and exposure to AbbVie's larger platform.
Abbott is mentioned only as AbbVie's parent company prior to the 2013 spin-off. The article does not provide information suggesting positive or negative implications for Abbott from this acquisition.
